newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 30.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wenesday's Daily Variety:
* The May sweeps have begun with lots of surprises, but none big enough to knock General Electric's NBC off the first-place spot for the April 21-27 primetime Nielsens week.

* The acquisition of Metromedia's entertainment group will accelerate Metro-Goldwyn Mayer's plans for a public offering on the U.S. stock market, Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes indicated Tuesday.

* EchoStar Communications Chairman Charlie Ergen said Tuesday he was "hopeful" his $1.7 billion satellite TV deal with News Corp would go ahead, but acknowledged vulnerabilities facing "little fledging satellite guys" doing business with multibillion-dollar companies.

* Despite a slump in the North American music market, 1996 was a period of growth for the international music industry, with world sales up 5.5 percent to $39.8 billion on 4 billion units sold, according to figures released on Tuesday.
* Robert De Niro and Jane Rosenthal's Tribeca Productions has named Brad Epstein to the newly created post of president of production.

* Confusion over the definition of various contract-related words in Hollywood has prompted a growing number of represenatives to insist on attachment agreements before their clients' names can be associated with a project.

* In the wake of company founder James Edwards Jr.'s death Saturday, the privately-held Edwards theater circuit has unveiled an ambitious cinema building plan calling for 18 new multiplexes to open in the next 12 months.
